22:1.sourceText: Ἤγγιζεν δὲ ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν ἀζύμων ἡ λεγομένη Πάσχα.
22:1.targetText: And the Celebration of the Unleavened [Bread] was coming near, that is called Passover,

groups.note: Actual article plus substantival neuter-plural unleavened adjective names the unleavened festival/food. English spells out Unleavened [Bread]; no independently written ἄρτος bread noun is invented.

22:2.sourceText: καὶ ἐζήτουν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τὸ πῶς ἀνέλωσιν αὐτόν· ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ τὸν λαόν.
22:2.targetText: and the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they may take Him up, for they were afraid of the people.

groups.note: Actual ἀνέλωσιν is the ἀναιρέω removal/killing predicate. The primary Mounce entry attests take-up/take-away/put-to-death senses and specifically the killing sense at Luke22:2. LSV retains the English wording take ... up; no separately printed plain take verb, up particle or change to the actual source lemma is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual τό introduces the how-to-do indirect question. English gives how directly without a separately rendered article.

22:3.sourceText: Εἰσῆλθεν δὲ Σατανᾶς εἰς Ἰούδαν τὸν καλούμενον Ἰσκαριώτην, ὄντα ἐκ τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ τῶν δώδεκα·
22:3.targetText: And Satan entered into Judas, who is surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the Twelve,

groups.note: Actual καλούμενον is the plain calling/naming participle. TR has ἐπικαλούμενον; English uses is surnamed for the named Iscariot epithet, without substituting the TR prefixed lemma or assigning the auxiliary to the article.

22:4.sourceText: καὶ ἀπελθὼν συνελάλησεν τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ στρατηγοῖς τὸ πῶς αὐτοῖς παραδῷ αὐτόν.
22:4.targetText: and he, having gone away, spoke with the chief priests and the magistrates, how he might deliver Him up to them,

unmappedSource.reason: Actual τό introduces the indirect how question. English renders how without a separate article.

22:5.sourceText: καὶ ἐχάρησαν, καὶ συνέθεντο αὐτῷ ἀργύριον δοῦναι.
22:5.targetText: and they rejoiced, and covenanted to give him money,

22:6.sourceText: καὶ ἐξωμολόγησεν, καὶ ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν τοῦ παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν ἄτερ ὄχλου αὐτοῖς.
22:6.targetText: and he agreed, and was seeking a favorable season to deliver Him up to them without tumult.

groups.note: Actual ὄχλος is the crowd/mob noun. The primary Mounce entry specifically attests the implied tumult/uproar sense at Luke22:6; English tumult retains that attested metonymy without a separately printed commotion noun or a universal crowd=tumult rule.

22:7.sourceText: Ἦλθεν δὲ ἡ ἡμέρα τῶν ἀζύμων, ᾗ ἔδει θύεσθαι τὸ πάσχα·

groups.note: Actual article plus substantival unleavened adjective names the festival. English supplies the conventional [Bread] component of that name; no independent ἄρτος noun is claimed.
Actual dative relative ᾗ provides the day/occasion relation. English uses in which; TR additionally prints ἐν, but no separate N1904 preposition is invented.

Actual accusative Passover phrase is subject of the passive sacrificing infinitive. English introduces that same infinitival subject with [for]; no independent Greek for preposition or different victim is claimed.

22:8.sourceText: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάνην εἰπών Πορευθέντες ἑτοιμάσατε ἡμῖν τὸ πάσχα, ἵνα φάγωμεν.

22:9.sourceText: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ποῦ θέλεις ἑτοιμάσωμεν;
22:9.targetText: and they said to Him, “Where do You will that we might prepare?”

groups.note: Actual ἑτοιμάσωμεν is the aorist subjunctive preparation predicate under the wanting question. English uses the finite that-we-might-prepare complement; no independently written Greek that conjunction or personal we pronoun is invented.

22:10.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἰδοὺ εἰσελθόντων ὑμῶν εἰς τὴν πόλιν συναντήσει ὑμῖν ἄνθρωπος κεράμιον ὕδατος βαστάζων· ἀκολουθήσατε αὐτῷ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν εἰς ἣν εἰσπορεύεται·

groups.note: Actual genitive-absolute entering participle supplies the temporal frame. English nominalizes it as in your entering; no independent Greek in preposition or finite entering verb is claimed.

Actual city identifies both the entering destination and the immediate encounter location in the same instruction. English resumes that same city as there after will meet you. Neither N1904 nor checked TR prints an independent ἐκεῖ word here; no extra adverb or new place identity is invented.
Actual εἰς ἣν is the into-which relative place phrase. English condenses that same destination relation to where; no different Greek locative adverb is substituted.

22:11.sourceText: καὶ ἐρεῖτε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ τῆς οἰκίας Λέγει σοι ὁ Διδάσκαλος Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμα ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω;

groups.note: Actual οἰκοδεσπότῃ is the householder/master compound in the dative phrase. English uses to the master and renders the following separately written house genitive in its own phrase; no plain δεσπότης source lemma is substituted.

22:12.sourceText: κἀκεῖνος ὑμῖν δείξει ἀνάγαιον μέγα ἐστρωμένον· ἐκεῖ ἑτοιμάσατε.

22:14.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡ ὥρα, ἀνέπεσεν, καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι σὺν αὐτῷ.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly adds δώδεκα before apostles. Pinned N1904 prints no numerical word in this verse.

22:15.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπεθύμησα τοῦτο τὸ πάσχα φαγεῖν μεθ’ ὑμῶν πρὸ τοῦ με παθεῖν·

Actual παθεῖν is the suffering infinitive. English uses the verbal noun suffering in before-My-suffering; no independent Greek πάθος noun or finite verb is substituted.

22:16.sourceText: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ φάγω αὐτὸ ἕως ὅτου πληρωθῇ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ.

Actual αὐτό is the accusative eating object; TR has ἐξ αὐτοῦ. English uses the partitive eating-of-it formulation for the same Passover object, without relabeling the source as genitive or claiming a printed N1904 ἐκ preposition.

22:17.sourceText: καὶ δεξάμενος ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας εἶπεν Λάβετε τοῦτο καὶ διαμερίσατε εἰς ἑαυτούς·

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν states from now onward in N1904. TR and LSV omit that temporal phrase here; its actual now word is not silently dropped or assigned to a different time expression.

22:19.sourceText: καὶ λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν διδόμενον· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.

Actual neuter demonstrative τοῦτο names the action at issue. English expands it as this thing; no independently written Greek thing noun is claimed.
